title: 2001 Ichiro Suzuki Game-Used, Signed Rookie Season Seattle Mariners Home Jersey
provenance: Letter of Provenance from Yu Fukushima
description_block: Ichiro Suzuki's legacy as Japan's greatest baseball product has finally been challenged by the utter dominance of Shohei Ohtani in today's game, but that shouldn't discredit the immediate impact Ichiro had on the sport when he arrived in North America ahead of the 2001 MLB season. Barred from joining Major League Baseball until 2001, Ichiro—who was just elected to baseball's Hall of Fame on his first ballot with 99.7% of the vote on Jan. 21, 2025—arrived with a slew of accolades and hardware, including seven Golden Glove Awards in Japan, three Pacific League MVPs, and a pair of Matsutaro Shoriki Awards. After his first season in Major League Baseball, Ichiro collected additional hardware in the form of the American League Rookie of the Year and MVP (the first and only player since Fred Lynn in 1975 to win both honors in a single season), a Gold Glove, and a Silver Slugger. Presented is a 2001 Ichiro Suzuki game-used Seattle Mariners home baseball jersey. To say Ichiro exceeded expectations would be a severe understatement. In 157 games with the Seattle Mariners during his debut campaign, Ichiro won the batting title with a .350 batting average and a league-leading 242 hits, as well as leading the league with 56 stolen bases. It wasn't long until Ichiro became an international sensation; when Major League Baseball allowed All-Star voting in Japan, Ichiro became the first rookie in baseball history to lead all players in All-Star Game voting. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. A 2001 MLB All-Star Game patch, commemorating the Midsummer Classic as it was hosted in Seattle that season, rests on the jersey's left sleeve. An American League centennial patch sits opposite on the right sleeve. The front left tail of the jersey contains a Russell Athletic MLB Authentic Collection manufacturer's tag with attached size "48" and "2001" flags. Affixed to the back of the jersey's collar is an MLB Batter logo. The jersey has been signed by Ichiro, who has penned his flowing signature in silver marker within the "5" of the number "51" on the jersey's back. According to MEARS, the jersey exhibits evidence of Moderate use with wear consistent with player and position. Also, according to MEARS, the lack of a USA flag patch on the back of the jersey "indicates jersey was worn prior to 09/11." LOA from MEARS (322164) with the highest possible grade of A10 for game use. Letter of Provenance from Yu Fukushima for authenticity. COA from Mill Creek Sports for game use and signature. Please note MEARS has evaluated and deemed this item as "game-used" with the grade of A10. MEARS evaluates game-used jerseys based on a 1-10 grading scale, with points assigned for attributes that include tagging, lettering, numbering, size, patches, materials, style, as well as provenance, supporting imagery, wear, and use. However, this designation from MEARS neither confirms nor guarantees a photo-match result. The sale of this lot is on an "as-is" basis, and the sale is final.

title: 1985-86 Michael Jordan Game-Used, Apparent Photo-Matched, Twice-Signed Nike Air Jordan 1 Sneakers - Post Injury - Sports Investors LOA, JSA LOA, Beckett LOA (2) on Goldin Auctions
description_block: NBA icon, Hall of Famer, and basketball icon Michael Jordan, returning from a fractured navicular bone in his left foot suffered in the third game of the season, used this pair of Nike Air Jordan 1 basketball sneakers during the 1985-86 NBA regular season, his second season with the Chicago Bulls. Jordan's injury robbed the basketball world of what might have been an electric sophomore campaign; limited to only 18 games, Jordan made 7 starts and averaged 22.7 points per game with 3.6 total rebounds and 2.9 assists. Despite being without one of the most electric young talents in the NBA, the Bulls reached the Eastern Conference First Round; in three games against the Boston Celtics, Jordan averaged 43.7 points per game with 6.3 total rebounds and 5.7 assists as the Bulls bowed out of the playoffs. One characteristic that can be found within this pair that makes these sneakers so unique is the modification made to accommodate Jordan's return from injury. The sneakers feature a harness to provide support to his foot and ankle. Outside of these modifications, the sneakers exhibit all expected qualities that have made this pair one of the most recognizable sneakers in the world: a red/white/black colorway matching the primary colors of the Bulls and the Air Jordan emblem embossed across the lateral side of each ankle. Add the fact that Jordan has signed each sneaker, penning his flowing signature in black marker across the medial side of each ankle, and you have a pair of Air Jordan 1s personalized for "MJ" and by "MJ." The sneakers have been apparently photo-matched to a March 21, 1986, game by Sports Investors Authentication. A preview of their matchup in the first round of the Eastern Conference playoffs, the Bulls fell to the Celtics on that date by the score of 126-105. Jordan, in his fourth game since returning from injury, recorded 20 points in only 16 minutes of playing time with 2 total rebounds and 1 assist. While the lack of clarity in the photos prevents Sports Investors from being absolutely certain "that these shoes are photo matched," evidence of game use, as is consistent with sneakers worn during a single game, is certain: creasing and scuffing on the uppers and tread wear on the outsoles. Light decomposition in the black leather near the ankle is also evident. Very light oxidation in the midsoles, a trait common with sneakers from this era, is also evident. The interior of the sneakers is stamped: the right sneaker is stamped "13 ½ 850102-TYPS," and the left sneaker is stamped "13 850102-TYPS," confirming Jordan's characteristic of wearing two different-sized sneakers and that these are player samples manufactured at the Tong Yang factory in 1985. There's no denying the Air Jordan 1 is the most iconic basketball sneaker of all time, bold and innovatively designed to create a statement of rebellion and self-expression while ushering in a new era of footwear design ruled by the iconic Air Jordan brand. Such was the success around the brand's marketing that they blew past the expected $3 million in sales to net $126 million within the first year. Sports Investors Authentication considers the sneakers to be "in excellent condition compared to most Air Jordan 1 gamers" they've examined. LOA from Sports Investors Authentication (250622M1) for game use and an apparent photo-match to March 21, 1986. LOA from JSA and Beckett for signatures. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by JSA and Beckett. The LOAs will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

title: Bobby Hull Game-Used, Photo-Matched Canada National Team Jersey - Tournament Finals Game vs. Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976 - MeiGray LOA on Goldin Auctions
match_event: Canada Cup Final vs. Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976
description_block: The significance of the 1976 Canada Cup cannot be overstated. It was the first tournament that featured the best of the world's best in hockey; up to that point, Team Canada faced a serious disadvantage in international tournaments as they were restricted from using players from the NHL. Meanwhile, other European teams managed to circumnavigate this restriction by masking the status of their best players. This came to a head in 1970, with Team Canada refusing to play international ice hockey competitions until they could use their top players like European countries could. After years of negotiation, Canada agreed to return to international competitions in exchange for being able to use NHL players; in a further gesture of goodwill, the 1976 Canada Cup was created as the first international competition to meet these new agreements. With Team Canada now fully equipped with a team of amateurs and professionals of their choosing, they went on to display some of their best international hockey action throughout the six-team round robin tournament. When Canada reached the finals to face Czechoslovakia, more than 10.5 million people were estimated to have tuned in for the game (a number that was roughly half of all Canadians in 1976). Presented is a Canada National Team hockey jersey used by Hockey Hall of Famer and one of the greatest goal scorers in the history of the NHL, Bobby Hull, during the 1976 Canada Cup Final between Czechoslovakia and Canada, a best-of-three series that saw the Canadians sweep both games with a 6-0 victory on Sept. 13 and a 5-4 overtime victory on Sept. 15, 1976. Hull, who was accounted as one of the tournament's leading scorers with 5 goals and 3 assists for 8 points in 7 games, used this jersey during Canada's overtime victory on Sept. 15. Featuring sealed numbering, lettering, and team logos on the front, back, and shoulders, the jersey displays an alternate captain's "A" letter stitched on the upper left chest. Attached to the inside of the jersey's collar is an "AK" size "46" manufacturer's tag with wash instructions. The jersey exhibits heavy staining from use and comes with an LOA from MeiGray (160697), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to the second game of the best-of-three 1976 Canada Cup Final between Canada and Czechoslovakia on Sept. 15, 1976. The jersey has been photo-matched to a 1992 Future Trends Hockey Card #178 'Last Time for #9' and an 8-by-10-inch photograph of Hull celebrating a goal; both images were taken during Team Canada's Game 2 victory at the Montreal Forum in Montreal, Canada, on Sept. 15, 1976.

title: 2006 Roger Federer Match-Used, Signed White Nike Polo

Federer has signed the shirt on its chest in black ink. In late October 2006, after a ludicrously successful season that saw him appear in the final of all four Grand Slam tournaments (winning three: the Australian Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open), Federer returned to his hometown of Basel capture a title that was conspicuously absent from his sprawling trophy case: the Swiss Indoors. Federer had previously been defeated in the finals of the 2000 and 2001 editions of the event, and had only participated in the event one more time (2003) since winning his maiden Grand Slam event at the 2003 Wimbledon Championships. Federer—who was the owner of nine Slam titles at the time of this event—was determined to win on home soil, and he did just that, defeating Tomas Zib, Guillermo García López, and David Ferrer in straight sets before besting Paradorn Srichaphan in three sets in the semifinals. This set up a final matchup with the tournament's reigning champion, Fernando González. Federer defeated the Chilean in three straight sets, winning his first title at the Swiss event. He would go on to win the tournament nine additional times (including in 2019, when his straight sets victory over Alex de Minaur served as the final ATP title of his career), an all-time record at the event. This was Federer's 11th title of 2006 and the 44th of his career. The offered match-used Federer Nike polo is white with black stripes at the shoulders and on the lower back. The size-large shirt features a black Nike "Swoosh" logo over the left breast and a three-button placket below the collar. Federer has signed the shirt directly below its three-button enclosure. The item comes with a COA from the Roger Federer Foundation for the use and an LOA from Beckett for Federer's signature. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by Beckett. The LOA will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

title: Michael Jordan Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed Chicago Bulls Home Jersey
description_block: The horizon of 1998 promised many things for the Chicago Bulls and their fanbase: a chance at their second threepeat of the decade, marking one of the greatest organizational runs in the history of the National Basketball Association while simultaneously foretelling the end of a golden era of Chicago basketball. No matter how you chalked it up, the Bulls' run through the 1998 playoffs promised to be bittersweet, regardless of the outcome. Presented is a Chicago Bulls home basketball jersey used by NBA Hall of Famer and basketball icon Michael Jordan in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals at the United Center in Chicago, IL, on May 6, 1998. The Bulls had already aced their first four games of the postseason, having swept the New Jersey Nets in three games during the Eastern Conference First Round before taking Game 1 of the Semifinals against the Charlotte Hornets. Jordan, to no one's surprise, led all players with 22 points in the game while adding a game-high 6 assists and 5 total rebounds in just under 40 minutes of playing time in the Bulls' narrow 78-76 loss. The Bulls would settle for the gentleman's sweep by taking the next three games to advance to the Eastern Conference Finals to face off against the Indiana Pacers in one of the hardest-fought series in basketball playoffs history. The Chicago Bulls' playoff run to their third consecutive NBA title in 1998 truly proved to be that dynasty's "Last Dance." Jordan announced he was retiring from the league following his sixth NBA title, a decision that would last until 2001, when he returned to the league as a member of the Washington Wizards. Hall of Fame head coach Phil Jackson resigned from his position before joining the Los Angeles Lakers in 1999, and the rest of the team was broken up: Hall of Famer Scottie Pippen was traded to the Houston Rockets, Dennis Rodman joined the Lakers, and role players Steve Kerr, Luc Longley, Scott Burrell, Jud Buechler, and Joe Kleine also departed. The Golden Era of Chicago Bulls basketball had come to an end. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. An NBA Logoman patch sits on the jersey's upper left chest, and the front left tail of the jersey contains a Nike size "50" manufacturer's patch with an attached "LENGTH +4" flag and "CHICAGO BULLS" and "NBA AUTHENTICS" tags. The jersey has been signed by Jordan, who has penned his flowing signature in black marker within the "2" of the number "23" on the jersey's back. LOAs from MeiGray and MeiGray Photomatching (157063), who have conclusively photo-matched the jersey to Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals between the Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets on May 6, 1998. description_block: Ichiro Suzuki's legacy as Japan's greatest baseball product has finally been challenged by the utter dominance of Shohei Ohtani in today's game, but that shouldn't discredit the immediate impact Ichiro had on the sport when he arrived in North America ahead of the 2001 MLB season. Barred from joining Major League Baseball until 2001, Ichiro—who was just elected to baseball's Hall of Fame on his first ballot with 99.7% of the vote on Jan. 21, 2025—arrived with a slew of accolades and hardware, including seven Golden Glove Awards in Japan, three Pacific League MVPs, and a pair of Matsutaro Shoriki Awards. After his first season in Major League Baseball, Ichiro collected additional hardware in the form of the American League Rookie of the Year and MVP (the first player since Fred Lynn in 1975 to win both honors in a single season), a Gold Glove, and a Silver Slugger. A 2001 Ichiro Suzuki game-used Seattle Mariners alternate baseball jersey and undershirt is presented. To say Ichiro exceeded expectations would be a severe understatement. In 157 games with the Seattle Mariners during his debut campaign, Ichiro won the batting title with a .350 batting average and a league-leading 242 hits, as well as leading the league with 56 stolen bases. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. A 2001 MLB All-Star Game patch, commemorating the Midsummer Classic as it was hosted in Seattle that season, rests on the jersey's left sleeve; when Major League Baseball allowed All-Star voting in Japan, Ichiro became the first rookie in baseball history to lead all players in All-Star Game voting. title: 1967-68 Dan Issel Game-Used, Photo-Matched, Signed Kentucky Wildcats Jersey

description_block: Yes, this is a photo-matched gamer from the University of Kentucky men's all-time leading scorer and rebounder. Period. Full stop. Dan Issel netted 2,138 points for Adolph Rupp's Wildcats in only 3 seasons (back when NCAA freshman couldn't play varsity) and without a 3-point line. There's even a fabled Sports Illustrated story about the legendary UK coach predicting that prolific future during a timeout. Encouraging teammates to pass more to the underclassman Issel, Rupp himself said, "This guy is going to be Kentucky's all-time leading scorer by the time he's through here. I thought you might like to meet him." Just recently, the University unveiled a brand-new Issel statue outside Rupp Arena! The 6'8 center/forward cemented his legacy in the Bluegrass State by dominating professionally for the ABA's Kentucky Colonels. He holds the record for most points in an ABA season (2,538) and ranks second-best for career ABA points (12,823). Issel's Basketall Hall of Fame bio describes him as "one of the hardest working players in basketball history…the model of durability and consistency." Hence Issel's nickname: The Horse. This spectacular sophomore jersey has been matched to uniformed UK portraits of Issel and apparent matched to multiple UK games. It features a distinctive "Y" in "KENTUCKY" (with a horizontal buckle or crease to the letter itself), as well as a noticeably small distance between the upper-right of the second "4" in "44" to the second "K" in "KENTUCKY." According to Sports Investors, the King O'Shea size-48 jersey is an apparent match to 3 Wildcat games: 1) Feb. 3, 1968 vs. LSU (against rival Pete Maravich!); 2) Mar. 15, 1968 vs. Marquette (NCAA Tournament Round of 16 with Issel's then-career high 36 points); and 3) Mar. 16, 1968 vs. Ohio State (NCAA Tournament Elite Eight with 19 points, 8 rebounds). Additional provenance includes a pair of signed 16 x 20 action photos from the Kentucky/Marquette game; a signed 8 x 10 photo in uniform with Rupp; and a pair of Polaroids showing Issel autographing the jersey front. One of the finest Kentucky Wildcat vintage gamers ever to hit the auction block! LOAs from Sports Investors (for matching), Resolution (for matching) and Beckett (for autograph).

title: Barry Bonds 600th Career Home Run - Actual Game-Used OML Selig Baseball
condition: light clay staining with numerous scuffs
description_block: Regarded as the greatest hitter in the history of the MLB, the story of baseball cannot be told without a chapter—or perhaps a few—dedicated to the greatness of Barry Bonds. It was on Aug. 9, 2002, a cool night at Pacific Bell Park (now Oracle Park) in San Francisco, when Bonds joined baseball royalty. Presented is the Official Major League Allan H. Selig baseball hit for Barry Bonds' illustrious 600th career home run off Kip Wells. The stage was set as Bonds walked to the plate in the bottom of the sixth inning with the Giants trailing by two runs against his former team, the Pittsburgh Pirates. With a 2-1 count, Bonds got a fastball over the plate and blasted the offered ball to deep center field, clearing the wall with ease. Bonds rounded first base with his pointer finger in the air, as 41,897 fans roared in elation. Bonds stepped on home plate with his patented double finger point to the sky. On his way back to the dugout, he blew a kiss to his family, who was sitting in the front row behind home plate, eventually getting congratulated by his teammates as fireworks erupted in the San Francisco skyline. The ball traveled an estimated 421 feet and was Bonds' 33rd of the 2002 season. With the homer, Bonds became the fourth member of the 600 home run club, joining Hall of Famers Hank Aaron, Babe Ruth, and Willie Mays as the only other players to accomplish the historic feat at the time. Bonds also became the fastest player in MLB history to go from 500 home runs to 600 home runs, doing so in just 240 games. Bonds would go on to win his fourth National League Most Valuable Player award in 2002, the second of four consecutive MVP honors. He recorded an unprecedented .370/46/110 Triple Crown slash line, leading Major League Baseball in batting average, walks, on-base percentage, and slugging percentage. The Giants would lose the Aug. 9, 2002, contest 4-3 to the Pirates, but Bonds walked away with a winning achievement, nonetheless. The offered baseball exhibits light clay staining with numerous scuffs throughout, and fading is present on each of the blue stamps. Affixed to the ball is an MLB Authenticated Hologram (MR024402) for authenticity of game use for this historic moment.

title: 2015 Wimbledon Novak Djokovic Match-Worn Dual Signed Adidas Tennis Shoes
description_block: Presented is a pair of 2015 Wimbledon Novak Djokovic match-worn, twice-signed Adidas tennis shoes. Djokovic has signed each shoe on its respective outside panel near the toe. The Serbian icon's 2015 campaign was one of the greatest single years in tennis history. He started off by claiming the Australian Open title over his opponent in the final, Andy Murray. He then snatched up titles at Indian Wells, Miami, Monte-Carlo, and Italy before losing in the French Open final to Stan Wawrinka. Next up was the Wimbledon Championships, where Djokovic was the reigning champion. The number one seed, Djokovic largely breezed to the final save for a tense five-setter against South African serve specialist Kevin Anderson in round four; he otherwise defeated Philipp Kohlschreiber, Jarkko Nieminen, Bernard Tomic, Marin Cilic, and Richard Gasquet in straight sets to reach the final against the king of grass courts, Roger Federer. The first two frames of the final both went to tie-breakers: Djokovic snatched the first one easily with a 7-1 victory in the breaker, while Federer outlasted his opponent in a see-sawing 12-10 tiebreaker to level the match at one set a piece. Djokovic—at this stage the younger, hungrier athlete—won the final two frames without the need of a tiebreaker to take the match—and the Wimbledon men's singles title—in four sets. His historic season was far from over, as he won additional titles at the US Open (staking his claim with three of year's four Grand Slam titles while making all four finals), China Open, Shanghai Masters, Paris Masters, and ATP World Tour Finals. He finished the season with 11 titles, including three major titles and a record six Masters 1000 titles. He went 82-6 in matchplay for the season, a personal record for single-season victories. The offered 2015 Wimbledon Djokovic match-worn Adidas tennis shoes are primarily white (in accordance with the tournament's dress code), with three black Adidas stripes on each side panel and an orange detail at the heel and tongue. The size 11.5 shoes feature Djokovic's personal logo on the outside ankle portion of each sneaker; the left sneaker features a white dove logo on the inside ankle portion, while the right sneaker features a Reiki power symbol in that same spot. Djokovic has signed each shoe on its respective outside panel near the toe. The shoes come with an LOA from MEARS (323138), which has described them as displaying "heavy" wear and assessed them as "Authentic." Additionally, the shoes come with two LOAs from Beckett for the signatures. Please note that this item is accompanied by an LOA from MEARS, which has deemed it "match-worn." Until Judge, the fastest player to hit 350 home runs in a career was Mark McGwire, who reached the milestone in his 1,280th career game. Judge, who hit his 350th home run—a two-run shot—off Cubs pitcher Brad Keller in the bottom of the ninth inning in a 5-2 loss, did so in only his 1,088th career game. A two-time American League MVP, the 2017 American League Rookie of the Year, and the owner of the single-season home run record in the junior circuit, Judge has fast-tracked his way to a spot in Cooperstown. The offered baseball displays surface scuffing and pebbling from game use. Accompanying the ball is a detailed Letter of Provenance from Jon Donfrancesco, the fan who caught Judge's milestone home run ball on July 12, 2025, at Yankee Stadium, attesting to the item's authenticity. title: 1973 Don Baylor Game-Worn Baltimore Orioles Road Jersey
description_block: Presented is a 1973 Don Baylor game-worn Baltimore Orioles road jersey. In 1973, Baylor's second full season in the Majors, the man known as "Groove" hit .286 (his best average as a member of the Orioles) with 11 homers, 51 RBI, and 32 steals while playing in 118 games. Baylor, known for his tendency to aggressively crowd the plate, was hit by 13 pitches throughout the season, the most in the AL. Baylor would later produce an AL MVP-winning season in 1979 with the Red Sox and made the World Series in three straight years with three different teams (losing in 1986 and 1988 with the Red Sox and A's, while winning '87 Series with Minnesota), one of only three players in MLB history to accomplish that feat. The offered size 42 Baylor game-worn Orioles road jersey is gray with black and orange knit neck trim and black, white, and orange sleeve trim. The stitched script "Orioles" and number "25" on the front, as well as Baylor's surname and number on the back, are all original, as are the full set of dark gray buttons that enclose the jersey front. A Wilson size 42 tag is sewn into the inside center of the collar, and a chain-stitched "73 Set 1" tag is stitched to the outer left tail. The accompanying William F. Henderson LOA (25-0813J01) notes that the jersey is "clean and intact" and that "the wear pattern of this jersey is notable (…) It is very uncommon to find a jersey like this with the original player name still on back AND showing as much wear as this one does, far in excess of what Baylor would have accomplished during its normal expected MLB life", adding an opinion that the jersey "somehow escaped the usual trip to the minor leagues, and I suspect it was perhaps worn as a souvenir by a collector/fan, washing many times over the years before today." The LOA concludes by saying "It is my considered opinion that this jersey was made to team specifications and worn by Don Baylor of the 1973 Baltimore Orioles."

title: 1948 Eddie Robinson Game-Used Cleveland Indians Home Jersey and Pants - World Championship Season - William F. Henderson LOA on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Former Cleveland Indians first baseman Eddie Robinson wore this Cleveland Indians jersey and pants during the 1948 season, the one that saw the Indians post a record of 97-58-1, with Lou Boudreau's team securing a World Series in six games against the Boston Braves for their first title in 28 years. Robinson was instrumental to their success, batting .254 with 83 RBIs and 16 home runs. As stated by noted game-used jersey expert William Henderson, '...but it is the finest example of an original Indians uniform from their World Series championship season that I have ever seen.' As the Indians were notoriously frugal and often recycled jerseys into the minor leagues, which were then worn to the point of destruction, the fact that it has remained in its original and unrestored state is a wonder in itself. The jersey is made of heavyweight wool flannel, typical of exemplars from the late 1940s. The seven-button jersey features navy piping sewn to the placket and collar. "Indians" is stitched across the chest in thick felt. The original Chief Wahoo patch is sewn onto the left sleeve. Robinson’s number "3" is double-stitched on the back in felt. Notably, the construction of the jersey is unusual in that it was made without any sleeve seams and instead has a stitched seam running up the middle of the back, a characteristic of Indians exemplars from the period. The inside collar features a Wilson tag with an adjacent white swatch labeled "48," in black. "Robinson" is stitched in cursive on a white swatch below. The jersey, especially given the Indians’ history, is in "very good condition," as per the Henderson LOA that accompanies, but exhibits minor insect damage, several small holes on the jersey where the fabric is perforated, evidence of moth damage, with minor foxing on the jersey. A few dark spots and holes caused by sweat and mold spores which occurs in storage. The pants feature a linen-lined waistband with parallel stitched "Rub Strips," designed to keep the shirt tucked in tight. A faint number "4" is penned inside one of the inner pockets by an unknown hand. A Wilson tag appears on the inside waistband with a size tag "36" adjacent. The pants exhibit wear and stress around the pocket edges, some red fabric staining at the leg openings from the socks, and multiple major team repairs to the right knee. Still, when one considers the rarity of an Indians uniform from the period and its condition, this makes the perfect addition to any serious game-used collection. Accompanied by an LOA from noted game-used jersey expert Bill Henderson for the game use.

title: 1969 Dave Leonhard Game-Used Baltimore Orioles Home Jersey - William F. Henderson LOA on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Presented is a Baltimore Orioles home baseball jersey used by former Orioles relief pitcher Dave Leonhard during the 1969 MLB regular season, arguably the finest season of his brief 6-year career. Leonhard was a staple in the Orioles bullpen (even making three starts) while pitching to a 7-4 record with a 2.49 earned run average in 94.0 innings pitched. The Orioles were the team to beat in the junior circuit that year; with 109 wins, Earl Weaver's club swept the Minnesota Twins in three games during the American League Championship Series before losing to the "Amazin'" New York Mets in five games. The offered jersey features all lettering and numbering in tackle twill. An original MLB 100th Anniversary patch is sewn on the jersey's left sleeve; in William F. Henderson's evaluation of the jersey, Henderson notes that the patch "is an original (not reproduction) patch but has been re-sewn on the sleeve slightly below the outline of the original one that would have been there." Due to the standard practice of reusing these jerseys during 1970 spring training or reissuing the jerseys to the minor leagues, the patch was most likely removed following the conclusion of the 1969 season. A Wilson size "42" locker tag is embroidered on the jersey's front left tail above a square fabric swatch "1969 set 1" hand-chain stitched in black thread. Per Henderson's evaluation, "This jersey has been restored with Leonhard's player name and number." A light table examination of the jersey reveals the number had once been changed to the number "70," which Henderson thinks indicates the jersey is "almost certainly a spring training re-issue, as numbers this high were generally not used in the regular season in either the majors or minors." Henderson concludes his evaluation with, "This is pitcher Dave Leonhard's 1969 home game-worn Orioles jersey, with its original tagging and front cresting, showing a restored player name on back and restored numbers on both front and back." Accompanying the jersey is an LOA from William F. Henderson (25-0616J01) for authenticity.

title: 1985 Pete Rose Signed Cincinnati Reds Home Game Jersey with Pants - William F. Henderson LOA, Beckett LOA
description_block: A 1985 Pete Rose Cincinnati Reds home game jersey and pair of pants are presented. In the twilight of his career at the age of 44, the 1985 MLB season marked the final season in which Rose recorded several accomplishments. It was the 23rd and final consecutive season in which Rose had at least 100 hits in a campaign, and it also saw Rose swat the final 2 of his 160 career home runs. On Sept. 11, 1985 (or Sept. 8, depending on if you adhere to the statistical error where two of Cobb's hits were counted twice), he surpassed Ty Cobb's all-time hits record with the 4,192nd hit of his career. 1985 also marked the final time Rose managed to play in more than 100 games. His retirement in 1986 saw "Charlie Hustle" set Major League records in games played (3,562), plate appearances (15,890), at-bats (14,053), and, of course, hits with 4,256. The offered jersey is a size "43" white pullover-style Cincinnati Reds home uniform manufactured by Goodman and Sons of Los Angeles California and featuring all numbering and lettering in tackle twill. The front left tail of the jersey contains a W.A. Goodman size "43" manufacturer's tag with wash instructions; Rose, taking advantage of the burgeoning collector hobby and the high demand for his own gamers, had the manufacturing company only tag the jerseys issued to him for game use with the size "43"; a true measuring of the jersey reveals it is a size 44. Adjacent to the manufacturer's tag is a chain-stitched year tag labeled "85" in red lettering, an uncommon feature for Reds uniforms from that year. William F. Henderson, in his Letter of Authenticity, surmises that the embroidered tag "was added after the fact, or perhaps by Rose and his agents trying to make their [collectible] look even better without regard to matching exemplars compared to other 1985-used Reds team jerseys." Accompanying the jersey is a pair of Goodman-tagged size "34" pants. The inside of the elastic waistband features a strip tag labeled "ROSE 34-28.5 ST 2 '85" in red numbering and lettering. The pants are of matching style and vintage as the jersey but lack any evidence of use. LOA from William F. Henderson (25-0813J02), who concludes that "this is a team issued and Pete Rose jersey from the 1985 season showing appropriate light use; the pants do not show use." The jersey has been signed by Rose, who has penned his flowing signature in black marker across the upper left chest; LOA from Beckett for signature. Please note that the item was recently authenticated by Beckett. The LOA will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

Chimaev made his UFC debut against Welsh fighter John Phillips. Chimaev smothered the Welshman from the opening bell, as Phillips scarcely spent a moment of the fight standing as a result of Chimaev's superior wrestling skills. The second round went largely the same as the first, with Chimaev securing an early takedown before securing a darce choke that forced Phillips to submit with one minute and twelve seconds remaining in the second round; the Russian-Emirati fighter won Performance of the Night plaudits for his efforts. Chimaev has yet to suffer defeat in his MMA career, reeling off 15 straight victories (including nine in the UFC), the most recent of which—a five-round unanimous decision victory over Dricus du Plessis—resulted in him winning the UFC Middleweight title. The event-worn walkout jersey is displayed within a 31-by-37-inch framed display that features a small placard reading (Khamzat Chimaev / Event Worn Jersey from UFC Fight Night: Kattar vs. Ige / In his UFC Debut, Defeated John Phillips via Submission / UFC Fight Island, Abu Dhabi – July 15, 2020" (the discrepancy in date is a result of the timezone difference between the United States and Abu Dhabi; the event's main card began at 6:00 AM local time in Abu Dhabi on July 16, or 10:00 PM EDT on July 15). On the jersey, Chimaev's nickname "Borz" (his nickname and a Chechen word for "wolf") is scripted in an unknown hand. The item comes with a COA from UFC (adhered to the frame's reverse) for the event-wear.

title: Virgil van Dijk match-worn Netherlands national team shirt

description_block: Presented is a Virgil van Dijk match-worn Netherlands national team shirt from the nation's June 10, 2025 World Cup qualifying match (in Group G of the UEFA section) against Malta at the Euroborg in Groningen, Netherlands. Van Dijk has signed the shirt in silver ink within the reverse-side "4" jersey number (the signature does display some degree of smearing). Van Dijk, widely regarded as the finest and most complete defender in world soccer, played all 90 minutes plus added time against Malta. After a pair of goals from forward Memphis Depay, Van Dijk scored in the 20th minute to make it 3-0: after nearly breaching the net with a header off of a set piece, Van Dijk scrambled to finish off the chance with his right foot. Never truly questioned in defense (Malta managed just two shots on target the entire match, versus the Netherlands' nine), it was an overall commanding performance from the towering captain, a two-time Premier League champion and one-time UEFA Champions League victor with his club side, Liverpool. The jersey is primarily orange, with a mottled black design around the collar, arms, and sides. FIFA World Cup 2026 Qualifiers and UEFA Foundation for Children emblems appear on the sleeves. Van Dijk's first name ("Virgil") and number (the latter including his signature) appear on the back of the size XL shirt. An "Engineered / VB543290R" tag is sewn into the bottom hem. The item comes with a MatchWornShirts NFC authentication chip (appearing on the inside of the bottom hem) for its use and signature.

title: 2002 Roland Garros Serena Williams Match Worn Signed Cameroon National Tennis Dress
description_block: Presented is a 2002 French Open Serena Williams match-worn Puma tennis dress decked out in the colorway of the Cameroon national soccer team's kits from that same year. Williams has signed the dress in black ink in the center. The younger Williams sister entered the 2002 French Open as the third seed behind the year's reigning Australian Open champion Jennifer Capriati and Serena's sister Venus. She breezed through the first three years, not dropping a set prior to the opening frame of her fourth round match against Vera Zvonareva (after losing the first set, Williams dropped only one additional game in the match). In the quarterfinals, she defeated wildcard Mary Pierce before defeating WTA No. 1 Jennifer Capriati in three sets in the semifinals. This set up a much-anticipated Williams vs. Williams showdown in the final, with Serena lining up opposite her older sister Venus (in their lone Grand Slam final match before the 2002 French Open, Venus briskly defeated her younger sister in straight sets in the 2001 US Open final). In the final, Serena marked herself as the player of the moment and the future, besting her sister in straight sets to win her first Roland-Garros title and her second major title overall. She would not lose another Grand Slam match until the following year's French Open semifinals, concluding a run of four straight Grand Slam title victories that was widely dubbed the "Serena Slam." This match-worn dress (paying tribute to the 2002 Cameroon men's soccer team, a Puma-affiliated squad that was playing in the World Cup during that year's French Open event) matches the style of outfit that Williams wore in the first two rounds of the 2002 French Open; thereafter, following mild controversy in the press, Williams changed to a black outfit for the remainder of the tournament (similarly, Cameroon was not allowed to wear its sleeveless kits at the 2002 FIFA World Cup due to FIFA regulations). Despite its brief usage on court, the Cameroon-style dress is widely regarded as one of the most striking and stylish tennis outfits of all time. The dress utilizes a sleeveless design and is predominantly green with yellow and red trim. A Cameroon Football Association patch appears near the bottom hem, directly across from a white Puma logo. A gold lion (a symbol of Cameroonian football) appears near the right shoulder, directly across from another white Puma logo. The Cameroonian flag appears on the back of the dress, near the collar. The dress comes with an LOA from Puma for the use as well as an LOA from Beckett for Williams' signature. Please note that this item is accompanied by an LOA from Puma, which has deemed this item as match-worn. This statement from Puma neither confirms nor guarantees a photo-match result. The sale of this lot is on an "as-is" basis, and the sale is final. Please note that the item's signature was recently authenticated by Beckett. The LOA will be pictured with this lot when it is received in our office; the document will be shipped to the winning bidder.

title: Circa 1969 Henry Jordan Green Bay Packers Riddell Kra-Lite Game-Worn Helmet - MEARS Authentic on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Offered is a circa 1969 Henry Jordan Green Bay Packers Riddell Kra-Lite game-worn helmet. Jordan—a five-time NFL Champion—retired after the 1969 campaign and was posthumously enshrined at Canton in 1995. Please note that the helmet was refurbished in 1970, leading to the original paint and logos being stripped off and replaced by a non-accurate green and white helmet stripe. A Packers "G" logo is present on the right side of the helmet. The ear pad is missing from the right ear. Jordan's number "74" is written with faded pen inside the helmet on a suspension piece by an unknown hand. The helmet is accompanied by a period 1960s lineman mask that was repainted silver at a later date and the mounting clips are broken. The item comes with an LOA from MEARS (321264), who have assessed the item as "Authentic." Please note MEARS has evaluated and deemed this item as "game-worn" with the assessment of "Authentic." title: 1975-76 Jerry Sloan Chicago Bulls Home Uniform Shorts - MEARS Authentic on Goldin Auctions
description_block: A pair of 1975-76 Jerry Sloan Chicago Bulls home uniform shorts are presented. Sloan, affectionately known as "the Original Bull" when he was selected by the Bulls in the 1966 NBA expansion draft, appeared in 22 games for the Bulls during the 1975-76 regular season and averaged 10.1 points per game with 5.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists. The offered shorts feature a white/red/black color design and are manufactured by Medalist Sand-Knit out of a mesh and elastic material. Bulls logos are present on each leg, and the inside of the shorts' waistband features a Medalist Sand-Knit size "34" manufacturer's patch, a player number "4" identification patch, and a secondary Sand-Knit "Designed & Tailored" patch. According to MEARS, the shorts exhibit evidence of Light wear. LOA from MEARS (322526), who have assessed the shorts as Authentic.

title: 1997 Jerry Rice Game-Used, Signed Nike Cleat - MEARS Authentic, JSA COA on Goldin Auctions
description_block: Presented is a 1997 Jerry Rice game-used and signed Nike cleat. In his age 35 season, Rice appeared in two games for the 49ers in the 1997 NFL season. During Week 1, Rice tore his ACL and MCL against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Rice attempted a return in Week 15 but reinjured his knee, this time fracturing his patella, ending his season. Regarded as the greatest wide receiver of all time, Rice is the NFL's leader in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns. The offered white, red, and black colorway left cleat features creasing on the toebox and staining on the heels. Nike Swoosh manufacturer's logos appear on the lateral and medial sides, as well as on the heel and tongue. Rice's number "80" is handwritten on the heel of the cleat in black marker by an unknown hand. Rice has signed the offered cleats, penning his flowing signature in black marker on the lateral side, including his number "#80." According to MEARS, the cleats exhibit light wear. Accompanying the size "13" cleat is an LOA from MEARS (322578), who have assessed the cleat as Authentic. COA from JSA (U23560) for authenticity of signature.
